_comment: Inter-region transfer where no per-pair API exists. AWS and Azure are
collected live; OCI is derived live from its egress parts.
GCP is the published VM-to-VM matrix, mapped to our regions by continent.
Value providers have NO dedicated inter-region rate: cross-region traffic
over public IPs simply counts as ordinary outgoing bandwidth against the
plan bundle, then bills at the standard overage rate.

gcp.unit_note: Prices are per GiB, not GB — GCP's convention, ~7% denser than it looks.
notes: Published VM-to-VM inter-region matrix, priced by source and destination continent; re-read 2026-08-18.
Per GiB. No free tier applies to inter-region transfer.
Hetzner's FAQ names it exactly: outgoing traffic includes "Other Hetzner Cloud servers with different network zones (eu-central, us-east, us-west, ap-southeast) via their public IPs".
Consumes the plan's bundled allowance first; the rate here is the overage ($1.20/TiB), mirrored daily by the live egress collector.
Traffic within the SAME network zone is free.
Cross-region Droplet traffic travels the public network and counts against the pooled transfer allowance, then bills at the standard $0.01/GiB overage.
VPC traffic is free only within a region.
Inter-data-centre traffic over public addresses counts against the pooled transfer allowance, then bills at $0.005/GB.
All public-interface traffic counts against the per-instance bandwidth quota, then bills at $0.01/GB. No dedicated inter-region rate exists.
